text:
maya: quick heads up — bringing up Helios-9B (int4) on dedicated pool. seeing two weird things: token aliasing around ids 19k-20k and apparent rotary phase 'warp' that makes long-context kvcache miss more.
alex: can you paste an example of the aliasing? :eyes:
maya: yes — small dump:
```
# tokenizer debug
19873 -> \"Ġterminal\"
29873 -> \"terminal\"  # duplicate surface mapping
19900 -> \"\u0120log\"   # weird extra leading-space token
```
maya: when we feed a long prompt (>=1024) kvcache hit rate drops from ~92% -> ~54% after the 2nd chunk. latency spikes too. suspect rotary indexing mismatch or token id shift in the kv/addressing layer.
sam: did you check embed projection ordering? sometimes int4 exporters flip proj dims causing subtle aliasing.
maya: good call. ran a quick compare of embedding rows between float32 and int4 conversion — many rows are identical but slices at offsets 64/128 are permuted.
```
# conversion command
python convert.py --model helios-9b --dtype int4 --group-size 128 --check-embeds
```
tess: sounds like two separate failure modes: tokenizer/vocab map issue vs headwise rotary index/kv offset. which reproduces on fp16?maya: FP16 clean — no aliasing, kvcache stable. only int4 path fails.
alex: do we use any custom tokenizer postprocessing for Helios? new merges or normalization?
maya: tokenizer is standard bpe with NFKC normalization. but Helios release notes say they appended a small suffix patch to the vocab for byte fallback tokens — maybe index remapping happened in the vendor convert script.
rachel: if vendor added surrogate tokens appended at end, and our quant export expects contiguous ordering, index space could wrap into rotary table bracketing. that would explain phase warp.
sam: can you dump rotary_table[:16] vs token positions where mismatch occurs? also check head_dim ordering (per-head vs interleaved).
maya: dump attached to CI run: https://ci.redwood/helios/33678 (ci-bot might have the logs)
ci-bot: Build 33678 — helm:convert-int4 failed. Tests failed: kvcache_integration, tokenizer_roundtrip, squad_eval (delta -5% EM). See logs: https://ci.redwood/logs/33678
alex: okay, squad regression -5% EM after int4 path. that matches aliasing affecting QA tokens.
tess: immediate triage plan:
- maya: produce token mapping diff between FP and int4 vocab export (owner maya)
- sam: run head-dim reorder smoke (owner sam)
- rachel: run small eval set with and without rotary scale fix (owner rachel)
- alex: check exporter code that assigns new token ids when vendor vocab appended
maya: starting token diff now. quick snippet of map check I ran:
```
# map probe
for old_id, token in enumerate(fp_vocab[:21000]):
  new_id = int4_vocab_index.get(token, None)
  if new_id and new_id != old_id:
    print(old_id, token, '->', new_id)
```
maya: found ~120 mismatches clustered at 19800-20050. many tokens moved by +1000 offset.
sam: that offset would shift rotary position if we use token id to seed positional aliasing in some exporters. do we ever use token_id%heads anywhere? alex: nope in runtime, but some convert scripts used token_id mod table_size to build direct lookup for rotary precompute.
alex: if converter wrote a precomputed rotary table indexed by token_id, and the vocab got appended, precompute table would be stale -> phase warp.
rachel: try rebuilding rotary table from final vocab ordering before quant export and see if kvcache hit recovers.
maya: doing that now. quick patch:
```
# rebuild rotary table
rotary_table = make_rotary_table(vocab_size=len(final_vocab), base=10000)
save(rotary_table)
```
maya: after rebuild + re-export int4, local smoke shows kvcache hit back to 90% and squad delta reduced to -1.2%.
tess: promising. we still need to fix tokenizer roundtrip — those token id moves are concerning for model reproducibility.
alex: long term: exporter should not assume stable token id ordering. add validation assert comparing fp_vocab vs exported_vocab, or remap embeddings rather than renumber tokens.
sam: +1. also add a repro test that runs simple kvcache smoke with 3 chunk contexts to catch phase drift.
maya: filing a PR with two commits: (1) rebuild rotary precompute from final vocab; (2) validation assert + roundtrip check. link: https://git.redwood/helios/PR-451
ci-bot: PR 451 opened by maya — running integration suite.
rachel: after PR, we should run a full eval sweep (squad, summarization, long-context QA) on int4 vs fp16 to ensure no micro regressions.
alex: agreed. add quantization group_size=64 and 128 runs to triage matrix.
maya: notes for follow-up: vendor conversion needs to either preserve original ids or provide a mapping file. i'll reach out to vendor eng. cc @alex
sam: thanks — good catch. :thumbsup:
maya: updating thread as I get more logs. will post CI links. thanks all.
